terminalTabs.openOnStartup.description: Reopen saved tabs when the window starts. Above 'autoOpenLimit' tabs this becomes lazy — the panel is shown but chats open on click (so 40+ sessions don't all load at once and OOM the machine).

terminalTabs.autoOpenLimit.description: Max saved tabs to auto-launch on startup. Past this, startup is lazy (show the panel, open chats on demand) to avoid a memory stampede. Set high only if you have lots of RAM.

terminalTabs.closeToDrop.description: When ON, closing a terminal tab removes it from the panel AND kills its tmux session (a permanent delete). Default OFF (safe): closing keeps the TAB — only the Drop (trash) button removes it. What happens to the session on close is then governed by 'suspendOnClose'.

terminalTabs.suspendOnClose.description: Default OFF: closing a tab only DETACHES it — its tmux session keeps running in the background (🟡), so closing/reloading never stops work and reopening reattaches instantly. Turn ON to instead KILL the session on close (🟡→⚪): a closed chat then costs ZERO RAM and cold-resumes from its transcript on click. Either way the TAB is kept. To free RAM deliberately use the ⏳ Suspend button on a chat (one) or 🌙 Suspend Closed Tabs (all). Only consulted when closeToDrop is OFF.

terminalTabs.autoSuspendHours.description: Auto-suspend a CLOSED tab's tmux session after it's been idle (no terminal output) for this many hours — frees its RAM while KEEPING the tab (it re-resumes from its transcript on click). Sessions doing background work keep their activity fresh and are never touched; only genuinely-parked sessions are reaped. Runs at startup and every 30 min. Set 0 to disable. The manual 'Suspend Closed Tabs (Free RAM)' button (🌙) ignores this and suspends every closed session now.

terminalTabs.closeDebounceMs.description: Grace window (ms) to distinguish a deliberate tab close from a window reload/shutdown.

terminalTabs.autoRecapOnOpen.description: When you open a chat whose transcript has GROWN since its last recap, refresh its AI recap quietly in the background (Claude → Codex → Grok CLI fallback) — keeps the searchable summary current automatically. A title you set by hand is never touched; only the AI recap text updates. The ✨ button is always the manual override. Set OFF to only ever recap via the button.

terminalTabs.showWorkingDot.description: Show a 🔵 blue dot while a chat's agent is actively working — streaming a reply, thinking, or running a tool — as distinct from 🟢 attached-but-idle and 🟡 detached. Detected by diffing the chat's visible terminal between polls (the on-screen 'esc to interrupt' line changes every ~1-2s while the agent is busy), so it also lights up for background (detached) chats and works for Claude, Codex, Grok, and Antigravity alike. A ⚪ suspended tab (no process) is never blue. Turn OFF to keep the old three-state dot.

terminalTabs.workingPollSeconds.description: How often (seconds, clamped 3–60) to re-check which chats are working. Each check is one lightweight terminal snapshot per running chat. Also the cadence for 🟡/⚪ transitions the extension doesn't drive itself (a chat's process dying on its own, another window attaching). Lower = snappier dots, a little more background work.

terminalTabs.workingHoldSeconds.description: How long (seconds, clamped 5–300) a chat keeps its 🔵 dot after its terminal last changed. Bridges quiet gaps — a long silent tool call, a between-turns pause — so the dot doesn't flicker; also the lag before 🔵 falls back to 🟢/🟡 once the agent truly stops. Lower it for a snappier drop-off, raise it if blue flickers during long operations.

terminalTabs.useTmux.description: Use tmux for live crash-persistence (macOS/Linux). Off = plain terminals.

terminalTabs.claudeCommand.description: The Claude Code CLI command used to start/resume sessions.

terminalTabs.defaultAgent.description: Which agent CLI a plain New Chat launches. Use New Codex / Grok / Antigravity Chat to override per-tab.

terminalTabs.codexCommand.description: The Codex CLI command used to start/resume sessions (must be on PATH).

terminalTabs.codexResumeArgs.description: Args to resume an existing Codex session. {id} is replaced with the session id. Tune to match your Codex CLI.

terminalTabs.codexNewArgs.description: Args to start a new Codex session ({id} replaced with the session id; empty = launch Codex fresh).

terminalTabs.grokCommand.description: The Grok CLI command used to start/resume sessions (must be on PATH).

terminalTabs.grokResumeArgs.description: Args to resume an existing Grok session. {id} is replaced with the session id.

terminalTabs.grokNewArgs.description: Args to start a new Grok session. {id} is replaced with the PTT tab id so recap/resume stay pinned.

terminalTabs.agyCommand.description: The Antigravity CLI command used to start/resume sessions (must be on PATH).

terminalTabs.agyResumeArgs.description: Args to resume an existing Antigravity conversation. {id} is replaced with the conversation id.

terminalTabs.agyNewArgs.description: Args to start a new Antigravity session (empty = launch agy fresh; it assigns its own conversation id).
